[NFCT.1.4.6] **A slot that names a unit converts a host's number.** A slot names
a unit when its declared type is a unit symbol ([LUNI.7.1]). Each call below
evaluates that slot's conversion ([RDSC.5.5.9]), taking `const ds_schema_t *`,
a `uint32_t` slot index, and a `const ds_slot_value_t *` and a
`ds_slot_value_t *` of the kind [NFCT.2.3] pairs with the slot's type:

- `ds_schema_slot_to_stored` writes the stored number ([LUNI.7.6]) of a number
  in the unit the slot names. It computes what `x::<unit>` computes ([LUNI.8.5]).
- `ds_schema_slot_from_stored` writes a stored number expressed in the unit the
  slot names. It computes what a kwarg of that unit receives ([LADP.8.5.3]).

Neither call changes the engine, records an event or asserts a fault fact, save
for an `EngineError` the conversion raises. The artefact has then lied
([RDSC.4a.9.3], [RDSC.4a.9.6]), and the call halts the engine and reports it as any
public call that raises one does ([NCBK.2.8], [NCBK.2.9]).
Neither is a `ds_engine_*` call, so [RARC.13.16] does not refuse one made from a
callback. After an EngineError each returns `DS_ERR_ENGINE_HALTED`, as the schema
accessors do ([NCBK.2.9]).

Each must return the status of the first of these that holds, and must write
`*out` only on `DS_OK`:

| Condition | Status |
|---|---|
| a `NULL` pointer | `DS_ERR_INVAL` |
| an EngineError has halted the engine | `DS_ERR_ENGINE_HALTED` |
| the index names no slot of the schema | `DS_ERR_NOT_FOUND` |
| the slot names no unit | `DS_ERR_INVAL` |
| the value's kind is not the one [NFCT.2.3] pairs with the slot's type | `DS_ERR_SLOT_TYPE_MISMATCH` |
| the value is a NaN | `DS_ERR_NAN_REJECTED` |
| the conversion raises an `EngineError` ([LERR.1.4.7]) | `DS_ERR_ENGINE_HALTED` |
| the conversion raises any other fault where a rule's evaluation would ([LERR.1.4]), or its result is NaN | `DS_ERR_NOT_REPRESENTABLE` |
